title: Set 196

sentences.ko: 저기요, 윗집인데요, 또 연락드려요. 난방기가 아직도 안 돼요. 화요일에 기사님이 오신다고 하셨는데 아무도 안 왔어요. 그분한테 한 번 더 전화해 주실 수 있어요? 밤에는 진짜 추워요.
sentences.text: Hey, it's me from upstairs again. The heater still isn't working, and I know you said the guy would come by Tuesday, but nobody showed up, so could you give him another call? It's getting really cold at night.

alts.text: Hi, upstairs unit again. Heater's still busted. Your guy was supposed to come Tuesday, but nobody came, so can you call him again? It's freezing at night.

Hello, this is your tenant from upstairs again. The heater is still not working. I understand the repairman was supposed to come on Tuesday, but no one arrived, so would you mind calling him once more? It has been getting very cold at night.

sentences.note: **come by** 는 잠깐 들르다라는 뜻이에요. **give him another call** 은 그 사람한테 다시 전화하다라는 말이에요. give someone a call 은 call someone 보다 가볍고 흔하게 쓰는 말투예요.
sentences.situation: 집주인이랑 고장 난 것 고쳐 달라고 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 이번 주말에 집 전체를 대청소하려고 했는데, 결국 소파에서 책 읽고 낮잠만 잤어요. 근데 솔직히 몇 주 만에 제일 몸이 개운해요.
sentences.text: I was going to clean the whole apartment this weekend, but I ended up just reading on the couch and taking naps, and honestly, I feel better than I have in weeks.

alts.text: Was gonna clean the whole place this weekend, but I just read on the couch and napped instead, and honestly? Best I've felt in weeks.
I had planned to clean the entire apartment this weekend, but instead I spent the time reading on the couch and napping, and to be honest, I feel better than I have in weeks.

sentences.note: **ended up** 은 계획과 달리 결국 ~하게 됐다는 뜻이에요. **I feel better than I have in weeks** 는 몇 주 만에 가장 기분이 좋다는 자연스러운 표현이에요.
sentences.situation: 주말에 아무것도 안 하고 쉰 게 좋았다고 말하기

sentences.ko: 자꾸 회사 그만둘까 생각하는데, 아직 옮길 데가 정해진 것도 없고, 잘하고 있는 일을 지루하다는 이유만으로 그만두면 좀 바보 같을 것 같아요.
sentences.text: I keep thinking about quitting, but I don't have anything else lined up yet, and I'd feel kind of stupid leaving a job I'm actually good at just because I'm bored.

alts.text: Thinking about quitting, but I've got nothing lined up, and it'd be kinda dumb to ditch a job I'm actually good at just 'cause I'm bored.
I have been considering resigning, but I do not have another position arranged yet, and I would feel rather foolish leaving a job I am genuinely good at simply because I am bored.

sentences.note: **lined up** 은 다음 일이나 계획이 미리 잡혀 있다는 뜻이에요. **kind of** 는 좀, 약간이라는 뜻으로 말을 부드럽게 해 줘요.

sentences.ko: 커피 들고 앉을 자리 찾느라 그 카페를 한 세 바퀴는 돌았는데, 테이블마다 노트북 하는 사람이 한 명씩 앉아 있더라고요. 그래서 결국 그냥 차에서 마셨어요.
sentences.text: We walked around that cafe like three times with our coffees looking for a seat, but every single table had one guy on a laptop, so we just ended up drinking them in the car.

alts.text: We did like three laps of that cafe with our coffees trying to find a seat, but every table had some guy on a laptop, so we just drank them in the car.
We walked around that cafe about three times with our coffees looking for a seat, but every table was occupied by someone on a laptop, so we ended up drinking them in the car.

sentences.note: **like three times** 에서 like 는 대략, 한 ~쯤이라는 뜻이에요. **every single** 은 every 를 강조해서 하나도 빠짐없이 전부라는 느낌을 줘요.

sentences.ko: 그래서 걔한테 말해야 돼, 말아야 돼? 말하면 속상해할 텐데, 내가 알고 있었다는 걸 나중에 알게 되면 그게 훨씬 더 안 좋잖아. 아, 모르겠다. 하룻밤 자면서 생각해 볼래.
sentences.text: So should I tell her or not? Because if I tell her, she's going to be upset, but if she finds out later that I knew, that's way worse. Okay, I don't know, let me sleep on it.

alts.text: Do I tell her or not? If I do, she's gonna be upset, but if she finds out later I knew, that's way worse. Ugh, I dunno, I'll sleep on it.
Should I tell her or not? If I tell her, she will be upset, but if she later discovers that I knew, that would be far worse. I am not certain, so I will think it over tonight.

sentences.note: **sleep on it** 은 바로 결정하지 않고 하룻밤 자면서 생각해 보겠다는 뜻이에요. **way worse** 의 way 는 훨씬이라는 뜻으로 말할 때 자주 써요.
sentences.situation: 친구한테 고민 상담하면서 결론은 못 내리기
